raw_response:
My whole life I have farmed this land. My father farmed it, and his father before him. I am 70 now, my back is not what it was, and my sons have gone to work in Shijiazhuang. I have about 8 mu left that I still work myself — I rented some out to the neighbor's son a few years ago because I could not manage it all alone.

What will I grow? Wheat and corn. Same as always. Same as everyone around here. I do not know anything else, and at my age I am not going to start learning something new. The wheat goes in the ground in October after the rains, and the corn goes in right after I cut the wheat in June. Same piece of land, two crops a year. This is how it works in Quzhou.

For wheat, I will use the Jimai variety the seed station sells. I have used it for several years now. It does well here. For corn, I buy Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — I get it from the supply cooperative in town. Everyone uses it and it gives a good yield.

My neighbor told me to put less fertilizer, that I put too much nitrogen. But I see what happens when the wheat turns yellow — I do not want that. So I put a bag of diammonium phosphate and some urea at planting, then top-dress before jointing. For corn I do the same. I do not use much potash — I never have and my yields are fine.

I will irrigate the wheat three times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading. Maybe a fourth if the spring is very dry, but three is usually enough. For corn, the summer rains usually help — I will irrigate twice unless the sky is generous.

I will spray for aphids and rust on the wheat, twice. Corn usually just needs one spray for stem borer or fall armyworm if it comes.

For tillage: after the corn harvest in September I will plough the field, then plant wheat. After the wheat harvest in June I use rotary tillage before planting corn — it is faster and I cannot do heavy work anymore.
